spans.s: The seasamum plant; नासाभ्येति तिल- प्रसूनपदवीम्
The seed of this plant; नाकस्मा- च्छाण्डिलीमाता विक्रीणाति तिलैस्तिलान् । लुञ्चितानितरैर्येन कार्यमत्र भविष्यति ॥

A small particle, as much as a sesamum-seed; तिले तालं पश्यति 'makes mountains of molehills.' -Comp. -अन्नम् rice with sesamum seed. -अप्, -अम्बु, -उदकम् water with sesamum seed offered to the dead as a libation; एते यदा मत्सुहृदोस्तिलापः
; Ś.3; तेषो दत्त्वा तु हस्तेषु सपवित्रं तिलोकदम्
. -उत्तमा N. of an Apsaras. -ओदनः, -नम् a dish of milk, rice and sesamum. -कठः sesamum powder (Mar. तिळकूट).-कल्कः dough made of ground sesamum. ˚जः oil-cake made of the sediment of ground sesamum.
कालकः a mole, a dark spot under the skin.

a disease of the penis, in which the fleshy parts become black and die off. -किट्टम्, -खलिः f., -खली, -चूर्णम् the caky sediment of sesamum after the oil is extracted; स्थाल्यां वैदूर्यमय्यां पचति तिलखलीमिन्धनैश्चन्दनाद्यैः

. -चतुर्थी The 4th day of the dark-half of Māgha. -तण्डुलकम् an embrace (so called because in it the two bodies are united together like rice mixed up with sesamum-seed).-तैलम् sesamum-oil; -द्वादशी The 12th day of a particular month (kept as a festival); तां रणस्वामिनं द्रष्टुं तिलद्वादश्यहे गताम् Rāj.

. -धेनुः f. sesamum made up in the form of a cow and offered as a present to a Brāhmaṇa. 'यावता वस्त्रेण कृत्स्ना धेनुराच्छादिता भवति तद्वस्त्र- पूरिततिलाः' is the another meaning given in the com.; भरणीषु द्विजातिभ्यस्तिलधेनुं प्रदाय वै

turpentine. -पर्णिका, -पर्णि (र्ण)कम् sandal-wood. -पिच्चटम् Sweetmeat of sesamum powder and sugar; L. D. B. -पिञ्जः, -पेजः barren sesamum. -पीडः an oilman; स्नेहेन तिलवत्सर्वं सर्गचक्रे निपीड्यते । तिलपीडैरिव
. -भाविनी jasmine. -मयूरः a species of peacock. -रसः, -स्नेहः sesamum oil. -होमः a burnt offering of sesamum.
तिलकः [tilakḥ], [तिल्-क्वुन्, तिल इवार्थे स्वल्पे वा कन् वा]
A species of tree with beautiful flowers;
; न खलु शोभयति स्म वनस्थलीं न तिलकस्तिलकः प्रमदामिव

. Kālidāsa describes the beauty of this tree as being akin to that of the saffron-mark on the forehead of a woman. The name suggests a relation to tila. the sesame plant, Sesamum indicum Linn. Now this plant has got flowers that have got a very pretty appearance. It is a shrub and not a tree. It grows four to five feet in height. Its flower has five petals. The lower petal is the longest. In wild variety there is a promiment spot on the longest petal which is highly suggestive of the saffron-mark on the forehead of a woman.
A freckle or natural mark under the skin.
कः, कम् A mark made with sandalwood or unguents &c.; मुखे मधुश्री- स्तिलकं प्रकाश्य
The ornament of anything (used at the end of comp. in the sense of 'best', 'chief' or 'distinguished'); कुल˚; जीवलोक˚
; यस्य न विपदि विषादः संपदि हर्षो रणे न भीरुत्वम् । तं भुवनत्रयतिलकं जनयति जननी सुतं विरलम् ॥
The burden of a song (ध्रुवक). -का A kind of necklace.
A kind of disease, the appearance of dark spots on the skin without any inflammation.
तिलकायते [tilakāyatē], Den. Ā. To serve as a Tilakamark.
तिलशः [tilaśḥ], ind. In pieces as small as sesamum-seed, in very small quantities.
. P. (तेलति) To go, move. -II 6. P., 1 U. (तिलति, तेलयति-ते)
तिल्य [tilya], a. Fit for the cultivation of sesamum. -ल्यम् A field of sesamum.
तिल्वः [tilvḥ], The lodhra tree, Symplocos racemosa; Mātanga.
